texts: When a Keeper fails a station, the Council judges that Keeper.
The Council may strip a Keeper of a station.
The Council may assign penance duties.
The Council may bar a Keeper from tending.
The Council has barred two Keepers permanently.
The two barred Keepers neglected the Sunken Cove station repeatedly.

fields.sentence: When a Keeper fails a station, the Council judges that Keeper.
parse: (: keeper_fail_judge_rule (Implication (And (Member $k keeper) (Member $f fail) (Agent $f $k) (Member $s station) (Theme $f $s)) (And (Member (sk_judge $f) judge) (Agent (sk_judge $f) sk_council_1) (Theme (sk_judge $f) $k) (During (sk_judge $f) $f))) (STV 1.0 0.9))

review.notes: Bare 'when' with indefinite participants correctly takes the whenever machinery — plain-variable premises, a per-occurrence Skolem consequent keyed on the trigger event, the During link, and (STV 1.0 0.9) — with 'that Keeper' bound back to the premise variable. 'the Council' is treated as a capitalized common noun (typed witness, no Name atom) and, being a singular collective, correctly does not distribute; fail/judge both take Theme by the does-the-object-change test.

fields.sentence: The Council may strip a Keeper of a station.

q2_gaps: an INDEFINITE ARGUMENT under a deontic modal ("may strip a Keeper of a station") — the norm reads as a standing permission over any Keeper and any station, but the only stated rule for an indefinite argument mints a witness, so the parse asserts one particular keeper and one particular station that the Council may strip; the kind-level reified-norm form is reserved for a kind SUBJECT ("A wheelwright must lacquer the spigot"), leaving an institutional permission with indefinite objects no licensed quantified form
review.notes: "The Council" is correctly a capitalized singular-collective label — common noun, witness, no Name atom — and "may" is routed to deontic (Permitted e) at 1.0 0.99 on a definite individual subject rather than the kind-level property form, which the instruction set prescribes. Theme for the dispossessed Keeper is borderline (a loss of office is a state change, arguing for Patient) but is covered by the stated "when the test is unclear, default to Theme".

fields.sentence: The Council may assign penance duties.

review.notes: Deontic 'may' on a specific (non-kind) subject correctly takes the event-level `(Permitted e)` at 1.0/0.99 with no tense atom; 'the Council' is a singular collective so it takes a plain event with no distribution rule and no Name atom, and the non-specific bare-plural object correctly stays the bare fused kind `penance_duty` with its head genus and no exposed noun modifier.

fields.sentence: The Council may bar a Keeper from tending.

review.notes: 'bar NP from V-ing' follows the causation-flavored-verb pattern exactly: a matrix event with Agent and a Theme on the reified complement, the barred Keeper's role placed only inside the complement, and no tense or status on the non-finite complement. 'The Council' is treated as a capitalized common-noun label (no Name atom) and 'may' takes the deontic Permitted sense on a specific act at 1.0/0.99, both as specified.

fields.sentence: The Council has barred two Keepers permanently.

q2_gaps: per-member distribution of a counted plural in OBJECT (Theme) position — the group + count + group-event + per-member-rule machinery is specified and illustrated only for plural subjects ("both dogs barked", "all the students passed"), so whether an object-position counted plural also takes the rule, and what shape its conclusion has (the matrix Agent copied in as a constant), is an interpolation the instruction set does not address
review.notes: "two Keepers" is correctly a counted common-noun group rather than a Name-only individual: the capitalized-plural Name rule covers a plural kind-word LABEL referring as a name, not a quantified plural. (Duration sk_bar_1 permanently) follows the duration-adverb rule with the surface adverb kept, and the rule's (STV 1.0 0.9) matches the plain-plural/count strength and 0.9 confidence.

fields.sentence: The two barred Keepers neglected the Sunken Cove station repeatedly.

q1_issues.issue: (Member sunken_cove station) types the named entity "Sunken Cove" as a station even though that name carries its own kind word "Cove", so the head noun "station" gets no witness and no link to the named place; the proper-noun-premodifier rule would instead give the station its own witness plus an opaque Possession to sunken_cove.

q2_gaps: Iterative adverb "repeatedly" on a SPECIFIC past episode: the frequency dial and its companion are scoped to the generic/habitual reading, and Every/TimesPer need a stated period or rate - so there is no licensed carrier. The parse correctly drops it, which is exactly the gap the instruction set asks to be recorded.

A capitalized plural kind-word label carrying a cardinal and a restrictive modifier ("the two barred Keepers"): the plural-label rule legislates only the bare name-as-unit use ("the Wrens beat the visitors" -> Name-only individual, no GroupOf, no per-member kind from the label word) and says nothing about whether a counted, adjectivally restricted use may take a group witness whose member kind comes from the label word - which is what this parse does.

"the <Proper> <lowercase common-noun head>" ("the Sunken Cove station"): the instruction set gives both the Brindle/Kestrel-River route (the proper noun names the head referent) and the Northgate-spokesman route (head noun witness + Possession) for this shape, with no test to choose - and here the two routes disagree about whether Sunken Cove is the station or the place it belongs to.
review.notes: The count/distribution machinery is right: exact Cardinality on the group, the descriptive modifier "barred" distributed by a per-member rule rather than predicated of the group symbol, and the distributive predicate keeping the group event alongside the per-member rule with tense inside the consequent. "neglect" correctly takes Theme (the object is not changed) and the participial modifier correctly keeps its adjective form.

issues.reason: 'Sunken Cove' is a name whose own capitalized run carries the kind word 'Cove' - which Core patterns says licenses that entity's type atom - so typing the same individual as a station asserts that the cove is a station, and leaves the lowercase common-noun head, the thing actually neglected, with no symbol at all.

gaps_confirmed: 'Repeatedly', an iterative adverb on a specific past episode, has no licensed carrier: the frequency dial and its companion are generic/habitual-only, Every/TimesPer need a stated period or rate, and the aspectual tags cover only again/still/already/yet - dropping it was correct.

A capitalized plural kind-word label carrying a cardinal and a restrictive modifier ('the two barred Keepers'): the plural-label rule legislates only the bare name-as-unit use, and says nothing about a counted, adjectivally restricted use taking a group witness whose member kind comes from the label word.

The 'the <Proper> <lowercase common-noun head>' shape: the Brindle-estuary route (the adjacent word states the named entity's kind) and the Northgate-spokesman route (own witness + Possession) are both stated, with no explicit test choosing between them.
new_gaps: Nor is it stated whether, under the Northgate route, the premodifying name's own internal kind word still licenses its type atom - here (Member sunken_cove cove) - alongside the head noun's separate witness.
adjudication.defect_summary: The compliant form is the proper-noun-premodifier route: (Member sk_station_1 station) (Possession sk_station_1 sunken_cove) (Name sunken_cove "Sunken Cove"), plus (Member sunken_cove cove) from the kind word inside the name, with sk_station_1 rather than sunken_cove filling Theme in both the group event and the per-member rule.
adjudication.notes: The tie between the two premodifier routes is broken here by the name's own kind word - a cove is not a station, so the lowercase head cannot be stating the named entity's kind. The count and distribution machinery is otherwise correct.
